docs.title: What is MiSAR?
docs.text:
MiSAR is an approach that follows the Model Driven Architecture to semi-automatically generate architectural models of implemented microservice systems.

A video demonstration of MiSAR can be found at:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sdRDkLesyS0

MiSAR consists of a parser that creates a Platform Specific Model from existing systems and a Model Transformation engine that transforms platform Specifc Models into Platform Independent Model instances. An instance of a MiSAR Platform Independent Model is the recovered architectural model of the implemented microservice system.

docs.title: Workflow Overview
docs.text:
1. Parse code → Generate PSM (Platform Specific Model)
  2. Transform PSM → PIM (Platform Independent Model)
  3. Generate UML diagrams (optional)

docs.title: Create PIM (Platform Independent Model)
docs.text: In this part, you will learn how to transform a generated PSM instance into a PIM instance using the MiSAR QVT transformation.

docs.title: Open Transformation
docs.text: Right click: MisarTransformation3.qvto → Run As → Run Configurations

docs.title: Select Transformation
docs.text: Choose: QVT Operational Transformation

docs.title: Input (PSM)
docs.text: Select generated PSM file (.xmi)

docs.title: Output (PIM)
docs.text: Choose output location and filename

docs.title: Run Transformation
docs.text: Click Run

docs.title: View Output
docs.text: Right click generated file → Open With → Sample Reflective Ecore Model Editor

docs.title: Result
docs.text: You will see: - Microservices - Functional vs Infrastructure services - Dependencies

docs.title: Create PSM (Platform Specific Model)
docs.text: In this part, you will learn how to use the MiSAR Parser to generate a Platform Specific Model (PSM) from an existing microservice codebase.

docs.title: Launch Parser
docs.text: Open MiSAR AIO and click Launch under MiSAR Parser.

docs.title: Fill Required Fields
docs.text:
• Project Name
  • Project Root Directory
  • Output Directory (where PSM will be saved)
  • Module Directories
  • Docker Compose file

docs.title: Automatic Importer (For Docker Compose)
docs.text:
When you add a Docker Compose file, the parser can attempt to auto-populate the remaining required fields.

When prompted, click Yes to auto-detect project files.

docs.title: After Import
docs.text:
The UI will populate: - Docker services - Module paths - POM files

You can manually edit/remove entries.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: If required fields are missing, errors will appear.

docs.title: Generate PSM
docs.text: Click Create PSM Model

docs.title: Output
docs.text: A success message will show: - File location - Output filename (.xmi)

docs.title: Graphical Model Generator
docs.text: This is the final step in the MiSAR process, where the recovered PIM is transformed into visual representations (UML diagrams) and summaries.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This step is optional and generates UML diagrams.

docs.title: Launch  Graphical Model Generator
docs.text: Open MiSAR AIO and click Launch under Graphical Model Generator.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
Provide the PIM file generated from the transformation step.

If you don't have a PIM file, you can simply change the file extension of the generated PIM file from .xmi to .PIM (case-sensitive) and use that as input.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• UML diagrams
  • Excel summaries
  • Architecture overview

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Useful for visualising system structure
  • Helps in analysis and reporting

docs.title: First Launch
docs.text:
When running MiSAR for the first time, it will detect missing dependencies:

Click Yes to install them automatically.

docs.title: After Installation
docs.text: A success message will confirm everything is installed correctly.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Ensure Python 3.11+ is installed
  • Ensure you have an active internet connection for automatic module installation

docs.title: QVT Setup (Eclipse)
docs.text:
This guide is for setting up the QVT transformation engine in Eclipse. It is not required to run the MiSAR parser or generate PSM files, but it is necessary for transforming PSM to PIM.

The QVT transformation engine is used to transform the generated PSM into a PIM, which is the recovered architectural model of the microservice system.

docs.title: Install Eclipse Modeling Tools
docs.text: Download Eclipse Modeling Tools package. Latest version can be found at: https://www.eclipse.org/downloads/packages/

docs.title: Import Project
docs.text:
File → Open Projects from File System

Select: TransformationEngineNecessities folder

docs.title: Configure Metamodels
docs.text:
Go to: Project → Properties → QVT Settings → Metamodel Mappings

Add:

docs.title: PIM
docs.text: Source Target http://localhost/mdd/PIM.ecore platform:/resource/.../PIM.ecore

docs.title: PSM
docs.text: Source Target http://localhost/mdd/PSM.ecore platform:/resource/.../PSM.ecore

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• QVT is already included in Eclipse Modelling Tools (2024-06+ until 2025-09)
  • No marketplace installation required
